Wales: A Motorcyclist's Paradise

Wales is arguably the best motorcycle riding destination in the UK. The Evo Triangle, Black Mountain passes, Snowdonia, and the coast road through Pembrokeshire offer some of the most thrilling tarmac in Britain. Welsh roads reward skilled riders with flowing bends, dramatic elevation changes, and scenery that rivals the Scottish Highlands.

What Welsh Roads Demand

Welsh mountain roads feature fast sweeping bends, blind crests, tight hairpins, and variable surfaces. The road from Llanidloes to the Devil's Bridge is one of the best B-roads in the country. The A470 through the Brecon Beacons combines long straights with technical mountain sections. Surface quality varies from glass-smooth to potholed within a single bend.

Best Bikes for Wales

Triumph Speed Triple 1200 RS — The ultimate B-road weapon. The 1160cc triple is thrilling through Welsh bends and the Ohlins suspension handles surface changes beautifully. Add a tail pack for a weekend tour of the best roads in Wales.

Yamaha MT-09 / Tracer 9 — The crossplane triple loves Welsh roads. Quick steering, strong brakes, and a characterful engine. The Tracer version adds touring comfort for longer days.

KTM 890 Duke R — Sharp, responsive, and utterly engaging on technical roads. The 890 twin punches hard and the chassis is razor-sharp. Not the most comfortable tourer but stunning on the Evo Triangle.

BMW F 900 XR — The practical choice. Comfortable enough for the motorway ride to Wales and agile enough to exploit the mountain roads. Electronic suspension adapts to conditions automatically.

Aprilia Tuareg 660 — Light and agile with a willing engine. Handles Welsh roads with surprising pace and the adventure styling means you can explore gravel tracks and forest roads too. Essential Welsh Routes

  • The Evo Triangle — A4212, A543, and B4501 forming a triangle of biking paradise near Bala. Fast flowing bends and dramatic moorland scenery.
  • Black Mountain Pass — The A4069 through the western Brecon Beacons. Tight hairpins, steep gradients, and wild ponies on the road.
  • Devil's Bridge — The B4574 from Ponterwyd to Devil's Bridge is a stunning mountain road with waterfalls and gorge views.
  • Snowdonia passes — Pen-y-Pass, Llanberis Pass, and the roads around Crib Goch offer dramatic mountain riding.
Welsh roads are heavily policed on popular biking weekends. Ride within your ability and respect speed limits, especially on the well-known biking routes. The roads are best enjoyed at seven-tenths pace where the scenery can be appreciated.

faq.q: What is the best bike for Welsh roads?
faq.a: The Triumph Speed Triple 1200 RS is the ultimate B-road weapon, with a thrilling 1160cc triple and Ohlins suspension that handles surface changes beautifully. Add a tail pack for a weekend tour of the best roads in Wales, from the Evo Triangle to the Black Mountain Pass.

faq.q: Do I need suspension that copes with rough surfaces?
faq.a: Yes. Welsh surface quality varies from glass-smooth to potholed within a single bend, so quality or electronically adjustable suspension helps. The BMW F 900 XR adapts to conditions automatically, while the Aprilia Tuareg 660 shrugs off rough tarmac and can explore gravel tracks too.

faq.q: Which are the must-ride Welsh routes?
faq.a: The Evo Triangle near Bala combines the A4212, A543 and B4501 into fast flowing bends and moorland scenery. The Black Mountain Pass (A4069) offers tight hairpins and wild ponies, the B4574 to Devil's Bridge is stunning, and the Snowdonia passes deliver dramatic mountain riding.

faq.q: How fast should I ride Welsh roads?
faq.a: Ride within your ability and respect speed limits, especially on well-known biking routes which are heavily policed on popular weekends. The roads are best enjoyed at seven-tenths pace where the scenery can be appreciated and blind crests and variable surfaces stay well within your margins.
